prompt.context: Our client is a US defense contractor and one of its divisions manufactures Apache helicopters for military operations. The company is considering setting up a new plant to meet increasing demand in the attack helicopter space. These helicopters are fully equipped with guns and ammo when delivered to the client. The client has considered three sites to set up operations: Brazil, France, and the US.
prompt.question: How would you go about defining the parameters for decision, and where should they set up the plant based on that analysis?

clarifying_info.q: How many plants does the client currently have?
clarifying_info.a: The client has 3 plants in the US: 2 in Kansas and 1 in Michigan.

clarifying_info.q: Are the existing plants operating at capacity?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the plants operate at full capacity today.

clarifying_info.q: Can any existing US plant be expanded?
clarifying_info.a: One of the US plants can accommodate an additional assembly line at a cost of $500M; the other 2 are landlocked in residential areas and cannot be expanded.

clarifying_info.q: What are the plant setup costs?

clarifying_info.a: Fixed costs are $100M annually in all three countries.

clarifying_info.q: What are the variable costs per helicopter?
What is the market size and revenue information?
clarifying_info.a: Defense budget for next 5 years: $100B (US), $15B (Brazil), $10B (France). The helicopter sells for $100M a piece. If helicopters are imported into the US, the US government requires certification at $15M per chopper.

clarifying_info.q: What share of each country's defense budget is allocated to our helicopters?
clarifying_info.a: US: 20% of $100B over 5 years. Brazil: 50% of $15B over 5 years. (France figures are not provided — star candidates will realize France calculations are unnecessary given relatively lower revenues and higher costs.)

framework: Export control restrictions: Assess whether transfer of military technology to Brazil or France is legally permissible; if not, US is the only viable option.
Financial analysis: Compare setup costs (CapEx), annual fixed costs, variable costs per unit, and revenues/profits across the three locations over the 5-year horizon.
Customers: Identify where buyers are based and proximity needs for design inputs and ongoing support.
Suppliers: Evaluate availability of spare parts, raw materials, and key components in each country.
Logistics: Assess complexity and cost of delivering finished helicopters to end customers from each location.
Manpower: Evaluate availability of skilled managers and technicians in each country.

questions.prompt: Calculate the 5-year profit if the plant is set up in the US.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify total US revenue, convert to number of helicopters, then subtract all costs (setup + fixed + variable). Only US sales are available to a US plant in this scenario.

math.setup: US revenue over 5 years = 20% × $100B = $20B. Number of choppers = $20B / $100M = 200. Total cost = setup $500M + CapEx expansion $500M + variable (200 × $15M) = $1B + $3B = $4B. Note: fixed costs of $100M/yr × 5 yr = $500M should be included if the candidate raises it; the model answer bundles into the $4B figure as presented in the casebook.

questions.prompt: Calculate the 5-year profit if the plant is set up in Brazil.
questions.guidance: Candidate must account for both US-bound and Brazil-bound sales. US-bound choppers incur an additional $15M certification cost each. Setup cost is higher at $2B plus $500M expansion at existing US plant is not needed (new Brazil plant is the additional capacity). Variable cost for Brazil is $20M/unit.

math.setup: US revenue = 20% × $100B = $20B → 200 choppers. Brazil revenue = 50% × $15B = $7.5B → 75 choppers. Total Revenue = $20B + $7.5B = $27.5B. Total Cost = $2B (Brazil setup) + $500M (US plant costs retained) + 200 × ($20M VC + $15M certification) + 75 × $20M VC.
math.answer: $16.5B profit over 5 years — $500M more than the US option

questions.prompt: Why is France not worth calculating in detail?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will observe that France has the highest setup cost ($3B), highest variable cost ($25M/unit), and lowest defense budget allocation ($10B), making it strictly dominated by both other options without needing to run the full math.

math.answer: France is dominated: highest CapEx ($3B), highest VC ($25M), lowest revenue potential ($10B budget). No need to calculate fully.

brainstorming.prompt: Evaluate the potential risks to acquiring (manufacturing) helicopters in the selected location (Brazil).

categories.name: Political & Regulatory
ideas: Political instability in Brazil could disrupt operations
Export/import control implications for defense equipment
National security concerns about manufacturing military hardware outside the US
US-Brazil diplomatic relations may shift over the 5-year period
Export control laws governing sales to both nations

categories.name: Operational & Quality
ideas: Quality of products may differ from US standards
Know-how transfer challenges in a new country
Availability of skilled labor and technicians in Brazil
Supply chain reliability for specialized components

categories.name: Commercial & Strategic
ideas: Cultural customs may affect business relationships
Labor reaction at existing US plants if production is offshored
Potential for selling to the worldwide market beyond these three countries
Currency and cost inflation risk in Brazil

recommendation: Set up the new plant in Brazil. Over the 5-year horizon, a Brazil plant generates $16.5B in profit versus $16B for a US plant — a $500M advantage — driven by access to both US and Brazilian defense budgets.
Brazil also reduces dependence on a single market (US), diversifying the revenue base.
risks: Political instability or deteriorating US-Brazil relations could jeopardize orders and export licenses
National security and export control restrictions may limit technology transfer or sales
Quality control and workforce capability may require significant investment
Labor relations at existing US plants could be adversely affected by offshoring
next_steps: Confirm export control and technology transfer regulations permit a Brazil plant
Assess US-Brazil diplomatic outlook over the next 5 years
Evaluate potential for sales to other global markets beyond US and Brazil
Model labor and supply chain risks in detail before committing CapEx
Explore worldwide market opportunity to further improve Brazil plant economics
